newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty plunges further vs basket, floor not seen.
newsitem.headline: Zloty plunges further vs basket, floor not seen.

text.p: The Polish zloty tumbled further in early Tuesday trade after sinking below the central bank's parity rate on Monday and dealers said that domestic bank currency-buying was fuelling the decline with foreigners idle.
Dealers said that unless the central bank intervenes to prop up the zloty more losses could be in store for the local currency, which lost two percent against its basket in a week.
"The rules of trade have been thrown out the window and despite the fact that this could be a good zloty-buying opportunity the market is selling," said Tomasz Nowakowski, dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
At 0800 GMT the zloty was at 1.47/1.69 percent below parity, against -0.75/-1.06 percent at 0715 GMT and Monday's close at an all-time low of -0.64/-0.73 percent.
It was at 3.4065/45 to the dollar, against opening's 3.3800/900 and at 1.9040/75 to the mark versus 1.8920/80.
Some dealers said foreign investors sold zlotys in swap and some forward transactions, which pushed the local currency lower on Tuesday.
"Foreigners are attacking the zloty though swaps and unless the central bank intervenes the zloty devaluation will continue," said one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw.
The National Bank of Poland will hold a news confernce at 1200 local time (1000 GMT) on flood credit for the government.

Finance Minister Marek Belka has said he would like to borrow more than one billion zlotys from the NBP, without increasing the existing budget deficit of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product, and borrow $300 million from the World Bank.
The central bank has often called on the government to stop financing the budget gap through the NBP because such lending propells inflation and money supply figures above targets.
On Monday the NBP chief Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz reiterated that interest rates may rise in order to cool domestic demand.
The money market tightened on Tuesday as players braced for a possibility of an official interest rate rise, aimed at neutralising the effects of additional government spending.
"There is no cash on the market and it could be connected to the central bank and uncertainty about interest rate levels," said Piotr Schmidt, dealer at Pekao SA.

At 0830 GMT overnight rates were at about 24.60/24.70, lower than opeing around the 25-percent lombard rate but up from 22.95/23.25 percent on Monday. Tomorrow/next were at 22.40/24.90 percent against Monday's close at 22.95/23.25.
